question.text: The equation of a stationary wave in a metal rod is given by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.002</mn><mo> </mo><mi>sin</mi><mfrac><mrow><mi>π</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mo> </mo><mi>sin</mi><mn>1</mn><mn>000</mn><mi>t</mi></math>, where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math> is in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>cm</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>t</mi></math> is in second. The maximum tensile stress at a point <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mrow><mi>n</mi><mi>π</mi></mrow><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mo>×</mo><mn>1</mn><msup><mn>0</mn><mn>8</mn></msup><mo> </mo><mi>dyne</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi>cm</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math>. What is the value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>n</mi></math>? [Young's modulus of the material of rod is = <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>8</mn><mo>×</mo><mn>1</mn><msup><mn>0</mn><mn>11</mn></msup><mo> </mo><mi>dyne</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi>cm</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math>]

solution.text:
y=0.002 sinπx3 sin1000t

dydx=0.002π3 cosπx3 sin1000t

∵ Tensile stress =Ydydx

The maximum value of the stress at x=1 cm

=Y×0.002π3 cosπ3

=8×1011×0.002×π3 cosπ3

=8π3×108 dyne cm-2

⇒n=8
